thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered: CANARY_EMBED_503S — 503 spike detected for /v1/embeddings (canary). Severity: P1. Trigger: 5xx rate > 7% over 2m. Auto-pages: mike (oncall) and eng-sre.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-78432 created and paged mike (oncall). Incident status: triggered -> unacknowledged.

mike (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it. starting triage — will check canary vs stable.

bob (eng-sre): looking at cluster metrics now. I can see a burst of `5xx` from the canary pool starting ~2:03 UTC. p95 tokenization latency also up. dumping recent logs.

bob (eng-sre): ```
curl -s 'https://telemetry.internal/api/metrics?service=embed-canary&range=5m' | jq '.[] | {ts, rate_5xx, p95_ms}'
# samples: {ts:..., rate_5xx:0.12, p95_ms:420}
```

carol (eng-runtime): saw a regression in the new kernel path in the canary build. There's a mismatch in kv-cache lifecycle that causes occasional NPE -> 503. Repro locally with small seq lengths.

dave (support): we're getting 6 customer tickets referencing degraded embeddings in the last 10 minutes. No billing impact but product impact is visible in search/recall tests.

mike (oncall): good context. Can we divert traffic off the canary while we investigate? want to minimize customer impact.

carol (eng-runtime): yes. recommend immediate traffic diversion and then rollback canary. Steps:
1) set traffic split to 0% canary
2) rollback canary to previous stable image
3) monitor for 5xx drop

bob (eng-sre): executing step 1. `redwoodctl traffic-split set --service=embed --canary=0 --stable=100`

bob (eng-sre): output: `traffic-split updated (canary:0, stable:100) — change propagated to edge in ~12s`

mike (oncall): confirm 👉 dashboards show canary traffic at 0% and 5xx for embed service already trending down from 11% -> 1.8%

erin (product): looping in product — prioritizing a customer comms draft if this persists.

bob (eng-sre): initiating rollback: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --service=embed --target=stable --selector=canary`

bob (eng-sre): rollout command returned: `started rollback: embed-canary -> stable v1.12.3 (requested by bob)`

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-78432 acknowledged by mike (oncall).

carol (eng-runtime): monitoring logs during rollback. I still see a few flapping canary pods during drain but no new 503s from stable. stack traces point to `kv_cache.free()` in the new kernel path.

dave (support): tickets updated: "We've reverted the canary changes; engineering is rolling back. We'll follow up once stable is confirmed." Customers appreciate the quick note.

mike (oncall): Can someone run a quick sanity on embeddings for a sample prod request set? `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -d '{...sample...}'`

bob (eng-sre): ran batch — stable responses returning, latencies at baseline. p99 still slightly elevated; watching.

carol (eng-runtime): rollback completed successfully: `rollout status embed-canary: successful; serving stable v1.12.3` — no new 503 spikes in last 90s.

mike (oncall): updating PagerDuty: resolving alert and setting incident to monitoring. pagerduty-bot, can you mark the incident as "under control" and stop escalations?

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-78432 status updated -> acknowledged -> monitoring. No further auto-escalations will be sent.

erin (product): good. I'll prepare a short internal blurb for customers and schedule a postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-sre + oncall tomorrow.

bob (eng-sre): root cause is likely the new kv-cache freepath in the kernel optimizations. filing a blocker ticket in backlog and assigning to carol for a patch: RED-ISSUE-1832.

carol (eng-runtime): will open a PR with a guard and unit test. I'll also pin canary build to v1.12.3 until patch lands.

mike (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 35m. @bob please take primary until the postmortem is done. I'll include notes in the incident doc.

dave (support): updating all affected customer threads with rollback note + ETA for postmortem.

mike (oncall): closing this Slack thread. If anything flares up, re-page oncall.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident thread closed in channel incidents. Reminder: create postmortem and link to PD incident #PD-78432 and RED-ISSUE-1832.
